item: A Stop is not a failure in thirteen more recorders (the R614 epoch, R617 PR B, R618)
summary: Each recorder now takes the R614 engagement epoch before its own switch check and reads kill_switch_engaged_since after the request, so a Stop (still engaged, or pressed and cleared inside the request) records nothing. Before/after: walk and warm read a connect the socket guard refused as the edition's WAIT_CONNECTION, now PAUSED_NETWORK_OFF (HTTP answers stay the host's); wiki track committed a revision whose text, diff or ORES fetch a Stop cut and moved last_revid past it, now it rolls back and raises NetworkBlocked (skipped_offline, asked again); the versioned pass cooled down and listed a cut fetch as an error, now it stops fetching with neither; ORES called a cut or by-name refusal a transport error, now refused_offline, with a redirect refusal (Q717's signal, the host's own answer) read before the Stop; the wiki stream counted a cut connection with backoff, now it does not; the markets pass and the import-all route read kill_switch_active after the error, now the feed's epoch; run_rule stamped fetch_failed on every rule after a Stop (Home: price feed needs attention, R320), now skipped_offline with no stamp and run_rules stops (the run-now route answers skipped_offline, still naming the switch; the consent-coverage probe pins the answer, the no-stamp test the rule), and the markets lane's rules_run counts the rules run_rules went through, not the list it was handed; a field-test step a Stop cut, or one started under the switch and cleared during it, was done for good, now it runs again; the items job and OSM replication read the epoch too. R618: in OpenTimestamps mode a Stop made custody write a permanent local-only proof, now it raises TimestampRefusedOffline (a TimestampUnavailable naming the switch; ots_stamp's own refusal by name is typed too, so a switch engaged before the entry's epoch was taken and cleared before it was read, which moves neither, is still a Stop) and the ingest auto-log queues the entry as owed for a later anchor, telling the refusal by its type: a flush keeps its one custody log (each refusal used to drop it, so every next article paid a fresh key derivation, ~173 ms encrypted) and logs one INFO line with a count instead of a WARNING per article; the drain stops at the first refusal (the rest stay owed, counted in refused_offline and still_pending) and the reconcile route answers it as the log route does, 503 in the refusal's fixed words, whenever writing was asked (a scan alone answers with its scan, the refusal in its drain's body), where the gap button read "Recorded 0 entries, each marked late." and hid itself (the button already shows a refusal's detail, so no UI string changed); back online, the drain writes each owed entry once, marked late, with its anchor; and the manual log route answers 503 in the refusal's own words, never a bare 500 (not-installed fallback unchanged); the ring loader had no switch check and recorded a cut candidate as its error, now a Stop ends the load with no error. Genuine failures with no Stop are recorded as before (a control test per site). Tests: tests/test_kill_switch_epoch_recorders_r617b.py (68); 56 mutants all killed: 35 on the recorders (epoch reads removed or reduced to active-now, loop captures moved after the head check, head checks, guards, break) and 12 on the custody follow-up (the flush's log dropped on a refusal, one line per article, the flush's line removed or at WARNING, the owed note skipped or removed, the typed match removed, the untyped raise, the drain count removed, an entry drained twice, the late marker dropped, a local anchor) and 9 on the read's findings (ots_stamp's refusal untyped, the log's type check removed, the drain going on after a refusal, the route answering it as a result, the second drain unguarded, a scan alone refused, the drain's count dropped, the field-test start ignored, the Stop read before an ORES redirect). Cost: a genuine failure that shares its window with a Stop is not recorded and is asked again. And the custody repayment is slow: the owed queue has no size limit, and the end of each collection pass writes at most 200 of it, each entry with up to three calendar submissions made under the custody log's append lock, so a large backlog in OpenTimestamps mode slows the end of collection passes for a while once back online. Release-notes line: Pressing Stop no longer leaves false failures behind in the Wikipedia, markets, field-test, items, map-replication, ring and custody records, and whatever it interrupted is asked again later; in OpenTimestamps mode the custody entries a Stop refused are anchored later from a queue with no size limit that drains 200 per collection pass, each with up to three calendar submissions, so a large backlog slows the end of collection passes for a while once you are back online.
